round7_force_servo.ruling_implemented: closed-loop grasp-force servo: per-side bias integral bias += k*(N* - N_side) on the 8 lift-chain joints (env side-bias support), position anchor at the press pose, anti-windup on contact loss, lift trigger = both sides N >= 0.9N* x5 frames AND mu*sum(N) >= 1.2W
round7_force_servo.variants: v1 command-follow relax (UNSTABLE: no position anchor, integral winds up, fingers flung over the top - anti-windup absent); v2 anchored + anti-windup 16 combos: no lift; PPO fallback 12 iters 30k steps: return -2.06 -> -0.94 (learning), eval peak 0.29-0.40 mm vs 5 mm gate - FAIL
round7_force_servo.key_assertion_test: Main's assertion (servo maintains N after micro-lift) HELD while contact persisted (N held 1.1-1.6 N through the trigger) - but the lift still stalls because of the cone-coupling law below, not N decay
round7_force_servo.cone_coupling_law: a pad contact contributes vertical drag up to mu*N, but every DOWN-dragging contact taxes it: N_strong >= (W + mu*N_weak)/mu. The left hand's F4 geometry taxes 0.34-2.5 N across postures; the right chain ceiling is 1.38 N < (1.47 + tax) in every achieved posture - the precise arithmetic reason all seven rounds failed
round7_force_servo.feasible_corner: N_left <= 0.3 N (light touch, counts for the contact clause) + N_right >= 1.12 N (within the 1.38 N ceiling): mathematically feasible (net surplus ~0.7 N) but not found by any schedule - reaching it requires force observation in the policy (obs pin 107 is test-locked; extension needs a coordinated test update) or the force-servo mode as an action dimension

round6_v13_flat_pads.question: on v13 flat face-parallel mid-height pads (12x12x3 mm, mu 1.8), does the systematic schedule x bias search find a >=5 mm clean lift?
round6_v13_flat_pads.answer: NO. 750-eval systematic search (schedule x bias, stop clause met) + 150 scouting evals: best balanced press 1.29/1.29 N, peak bottom clearance 0.003 mm, end-face ratios 0
round6_v13_flat_pads.drag_ceiling_law: the measured vertical drag ceiling across ALL rounds = min(curl forcerange)/arm = 0.159 N*m / ~0.115 m ~ 1.38 N per finger chain (v9: 0.74 N -> v12: 1.26 N -> v13: 1.2-1.26 N, tracking the cap). One-sided chain cannot carry the 1.47 N weight (short by 6%); BOTH sides sticking simultaneously = 2.76 N >= 1.47 N - the capacity window is PHYSICALLY OPEN
round6_v13_flat_pads.terminal_verdict: the lift gate is UNREACHABLE BY OPEN-LOOP COMMAND SCHEDULES in this scene - measured, mechanism-complete (r1 friction decay, r2 down-clamp wedge, r3 torque wall, r4/r5 position-vs-force trap, r6 flat-pad systematic sweep); 'physically impossible' would OVERSTATE it: the two-sided-stick window is open, but transferring weight to the pads requires closed-loop coordination (force-feedback observation or a grasp-force servo) that no fixed command schedule provides - the quasi-static equilibrium always returns the weight to the table
round6_v13_flat_pads.concrete_next: (a) pad normal forces in the observation + PPO with the corrected gate (the both-sides-stick window is the reward signal); (b) a per-hand grasp-force servo mode (position servo relaxed on the 8 lift-chain joints during lift); both are W6c-continued scope, not scene changes

round5_force_bias.result: NO clean >=5 mm lift at any bias up to the cap; with the bias the measured side press DROPS (3.4 -> 1.9 N) - on the v12 curl-chain kinematics, joint-space closing torque converts into pad ROLL (contact migration over the top edge), not contact force: force control at the JOINT is not force control at the CONTACT for rolling cylindrical pads
round5_force_bias.terminal_conclusion: per the r5 stop clause: bias swept to cap without a pass = the combination of current finger geometry (curl-chain-mounted cylindrical pads) and box friction is the physical upper bound for friction lift of this box; the lift gate is unreachable by any command/force schedule realizable in this scene
round5_force_bias.gpt_final_note: for the final acceptance assessment: 4 mechanism closures (r1 friction decay, r2 down-clamp wedge, r3 torque wall, r4/r5 position-vs-force control trap), ~4300 candidates total, every round's blocker fixed and superseded by the next; the gates that DID close: symmetric pinch touch (w6b), no-lift schedules are stable and slip-free (yaw <0.2 deg, slip 0)

round4_v12_torque_budget.question: with ffj1/2+mfj1/2 force caps x1.7 (hardware-spec, v12 XML f8925e27), does the servo-yield wall break and the 5 mm clean lift appear?
round4_v12_torque_budget.answer: NO - and the r3 wall diagnosis completes into a closure: the position-servo static trap. With the box at rest every static equilibrium carries the weight on the table; the stronger servos press harder (pre-press pair up to 2.7 N) but the vertical drag demand never reaches the friction cone. Measured (frozen fingers, pure wrist rise, N=1.7 N, mu=1.8): t_up = +1.25 N static (cone limit 3 N unused) while OTHER pads of the same press contribute a net DOWNWARD component ~1.3-2.6 N (top-edge/chamfer touchers) - net vertical stays below weight; and when a micro-lift starts the drag REVERSES (-0.6 N) as the springs pull the pads back down. The yield is a quasi-static equilibrium, not bandwidth-limited: snap lifts (2.9 mm/frame) absorb within 1-2 frames
variants_exhausted_r4: two-pad-only press (th/rf retracted - down-component still wins via the press geometry)
round4_v12_torque_budget.closure_statement: across 4 rounds the mechanisms r1 (friction decay), r2 (down-clamp wedge), r3 (torque wall) and r4 (position-servo static trap) are mutually exclusive and jointly exhaustive over command-schedule control: a friction lift of this box needs the vertical drag demand to reach the friction cone, and under pure position control the demand is structurally zero while the box rests. ~1500 additional candidates this round, ~3500 total
round4_v12_torque_budget.next_lever_needs_ruling: (a) force-controlled grasp: a constant grip-force bias on the curl actuators during lift (the standard grasp-lift solution; actuator-type change = W6a ruling); (b) velocity servos for the lift phase (same class); (c) renegotiate 'separation must be finger-driven' to admit momentum transients (the smoke4 flick class, currently red-lined); (d) lower the gate band

round3_v10_pads.question: does the 3.5 mm stall become a >=5 mm clean lift on mu=1.8 cylindrical (r9x11 mm) pads (v10-fixed, seed 4c7a86d surface-gap baseline)?
round3_v10_pads.answer: NO - and the mechanism CHANGED: the friction-decay stall of rounds 1-2 is GONE (lift-window normals steady 1.4 N/side, tilt 0.05 deg, pre-press pair up to 4.4 N), but the binding constraint moved to the finger servo torque budget: transmitting the ~1.5 N vertical drag through the curl chain demands cap-level torque per joint (0.09-0.105 N*m at ~45 mm arms), and the position servos yield first - wrist +9 mm produces only +1.4 mm pad world motion, tangential demand stays static-stick at 0.3-0.7 N, the box never unweights

fast lift 10-20 f (servo yield absorbs in 1-2 frames)
curl-close ramp (drags DOWN: closing moves the pad inward-down)

round3_v10_pads.scene_conclusion: on v10 pads the box cannot be lifted >=5 mm clean under the CURRENT finger servo force budget; this is an actuator-envelope constraint, not a friction or geometry one
